exposure: 24-hour urinary protein excretion during pregnancy (mild, severe, massive)
cohort: 293 patients with pre-eclampsia who delivered at a referral maternity hospital in Brazil between January 1, 2009, and December 31, 2013
finding: Women with higher levels of proteinuria during pregnancy had shorter pregnancies, higher rates of preterm delivery and severe pre-eclampsia, and were more likely to remain proteinuric postpartum.
mod_finding: The rate of cesarean delivery was above 80% in all groups, regardless of the severity of proteinuria in women with pre-eclampsia.
